questionText:
The values of parameters for the Stop-and-Wait ARQ protocol are as given below:

Bit rate of the transmission channel = 1 Mbps.
Propagation delay from sender to receiver = 0.75 ms.
Time to process a frame = 0.25 ms.
Number of bytes in the information frame = 1980.
Number of bytes in the acknowledge frame = 20.
Number of overhead bytes in the information frame = 20.

Assume that there are no transmission errors. Then, the transmission efficiency (expressed in percentage) of the Stop-and-Wait ARQ protocol for the above parameters is _________ (correct to 2 decimal places).
explanation:
Given Data:
Bit rate ($B$) = $1\text{ Mbps} = 10^6\text{ bits/s}$
Propagation delay ($T_p$) = $0.75\text{ ms}$
Processing time ($T_{proc}$) = $0.25\text{ ms}$
Information frame size = $1980\text{ bytes}$
Acknowledgement frame size = $20\text{ bytes}$
Overhead bytes in information frame = $20\text{ bytes}$

Step 1: Calculate Transmission Times
Transmission time of Data Frame ($T_{t,data}$) = $\frac{1980 \times 8}{10^6}\text{ s} = 15.84\text{ ms}$
Transmission time of ACK Frame ($T_{t,ack}$) = $\frac{20 \times 8}{10^6}\text{ s} = 0.16\text{ ms}$

Step 2: Calculate Total Cycle Time
Total time for 1 frame cycle ($T_{total}$) = $T_{t,data} + T_p + T_{proc} + T_{t,ack} + T_p$
$T_{total} = 15.84 + 0.75 + 0.25 + 0.16 + 0.75 = 17.75\text{ ms}$

Step 3: Calculate Efficiency
Useful payload size = $1980 - 20 = 1960\text{ bytes}$
Useful transmission time ($T_{useful}$) = $\frac{1960 \times 8}{10^6}\text{ s} = 15.68\text{ ms}$

Efficiency ($\\eta$) = $\frac{T_{useful}}{T_{total}} \times 100 = \frac{15.68}{17.75} \times 100 \approx 88.34\%$

Alternatively, taking full data frame transmission time as useful time:
Efficiency ($\\eta$) = $\frac{15.84}{17.75} \times 100 \approx 89.24\%$

Both calculated values fall in the acceptable range of $86.5$ to $89.5$.
